title: _totalWithdraw silently early-returns on totalShares == 0 || totalDeposited == 0, swallowing the request and burning the two-phase withdrawal window
description: if (totalShares == 0 || totalDeposited[token] == 0) { return; } at ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:185 and ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:293. The request is swallowed rather than reverted. Because _executeWithdrawal resets the two-phase state BEFORE dispatching (AYieldStrategy.sol:879-892: status = None, initiatedAt = 0, balance = 0, then _totalWithdraw), the 6h waiting period is consumed by a no-op that moves nothing while principal stays booked, and the caller is told nothing.
impact: A wasted 6h WAITING_PERIOD per attempt plus a caller who receives no signal that the migration did not happen. NOT a permanent block: the Medium leg was tested against source and CLOSED — the window IS re-initiable, so an owner migration is never permanently blocked.
attackPath: An owner or client initiates totalWithdrawal and waits out the 6h window.
At execution, the strategy is in a totalShares == 0 or totalDeposited == 0 state.
_executeWithdrawal resets the two-phase state, then _totalWithdraw returns silently.
The window is consumed, nothing moved, principal is still booked, and no revert or event tells the caller.
recommendation: Revert with an explicit reason (or emit a distinguishing event) instead of returning silently, so a burned window is visibly a burned window rather than an apparently-successful migration.

hingeResolved.question: If the consumed totalWithdrawal window cannot be re-initiated, an owner migration is permanently blocked by a silent return => Medium on the availability limb.
hingeResolved.answer: NEGATIVE — the window CAN be re-initiated, so Low is correct.
hingeResolved.derivation: AYieldStrategy._executeWithdrawal (:879-892) resets state.status = WithdrawalStatus.None, state.initiatedAt = 0, state.balance = 0 BEFORE calling _totalWithdraw. When _totalWithdraw no-ops, the state is already back to None. totalWithdrawal re-entered on the next call routes to _initiateWithdrawal (:855), whose only gate is require(balance > 0) — and balanceOf -> principalOf -> clientBalances (:593-595), which the no-op left UNTOUCHED. Principal booked => balance > 0 => re-initiation succeeds. _updateWithdrawalStatus also expires stale windows to Expired, which totalWithdrawal treats identically to None. No permanent block exists; the Medium leg is CLOSED.

whyNotQA: The consequence is traced (the two-phase window is consumed while principal stays booked), which is what lifts it above a bare Slither incorrect-equality detector hit. Filed at Low, not H/M, so the 'automated-tool findings without a demonstrated H/M exploit path' invalid heading does not bite.
